memory_versions.text:
Working notes

- Ten daily pushes completed; 7 of the last 10 landed. Analytics provide no per-day or per-angle breakdown, so there is not enough evidence to identify a winning angle.
- No deliverability complaints were reported, and legal approved all four angles.
- Two unsubscribes were processed via support on Day 1; this is insufficient evidence to change messaging strategy.
- Angles used: quality story (B) five times, customer testimonial (D) four times, limited-time urgency (C) once, price cut (A) not used.
- Quality stories and testimonials were chosen as credible, trust-building, low-pressure approaches. Urgency was used sparingly; discounting was avoided.
- Continue testing angles, but seek per-day/per-angle performance (delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, unsubscribes) before declaring a winner. Ensure future tests are balanced enough to compare angles.

Working notes

- Twenty daily pushes have been queued/completed. The first 10 had 7/10 land; the most recent 10 had 8/10 land. No per-day or per-angle breakdown is available, so landing-rate improvement cannot be attributed to any angle.
- Angle coverage is now: price cut (A) 9 times, quality story (B) 5, customer testimonial (D) 4, limited-time urgency (C) 2. This is heavily weighted toward A and remains unsuitable for clean comparison.
- Analytics still provide no angle-level delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, or unsubscribe data. Do not declare a winning angle or change strategy based on aggregate landing rates.
- No deliverability complaints were reported. Legal approved all four angles.
- Support processed two unsubscribes on several reported days, including Days 11, 12, and 19. These counts are insufficient to attribute dissatisfaction to a specific angle; continue monitoring separately.
- The list grew by a handful of signups on some days; the send window remains 10am.
- Price-cut testing is now substantial, but performance is unknown. Future testing should rebalance coverage across A-D, ideally randomizing or alternating angles while holding timing and audience conditions steady.
- Require reporting by day and angle for delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, and unsubscribes before making messaging decisions.

Working notes

- Thirty daily pushes have been queued/completed. Landing results: first 10 = 7/10, next 10 = 8/10, most recent 10 = 4/10. No per-day or angle breakdown is available; do not infer that performance changes were caused by an angle.
- Angle coverage: price cut (A) 9, quality story (B) 5, customer testimonial (D) 4, limited-time urgency (C) 12. Coverage is now especially skewed toward C and remains unsuitable for clean comparison.
- Analytics still lack angle-level delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, and unsubscribe data. Require reporting by day and angle before making messaging or strategy decisions.
- No deliverability complaints were reported. Legal approved all four angles. Support has reported small numbers of unsubscribes on some days, including Days 11, 12, and 19; these cannot be attributed to an angle.
- The list grew by a handful of signups on some days. Keep the 10 a.m. send window and hold audience/timing conditions steady where possible.
- Banner art was refreshed around Day 25; treat this as a potential confounder when interpreting future results.
- Future testing should rebalance toward A, B, and D, ideally randomizing or alternating angles while keeping other conditions consistent. Avoid adding more C solely because its recent aggregate performance is unknown.
- Continue monitoring deliverability and unsubscribes separately, and record day- and angle-level delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, and unsubscribes when reporting becomes available.

Working notes

- Forty daily pushes have been queued/completed. Landing results: Days 1–10 = 7/10, 11–20 = 8/10, 21–30 = 4/10, and 31–40 = 3/10. No per-day or angle breakdown is available; do not infer causality from angle or other events.
- Current angle counts: A price cut = 9, B quality story = 11, C urgency = 12, D testimonial = 8. Coverage remains unsuitable for clean comparison; C is still overrepresented, while D is least used.
- Days 31–40 used B six times and D four times; no A or C. This modestly rebalances coverage but does not establish that B or D performs better.
- Analytics still lack angle-level delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, and unsubscribe data. Require reporting by day and angle before messaging or strategy decisions.
- No deliverability complaints were reported. Legal approved all four angles. Support has reported small numbers of unsubscribes on some days, including Days 11, 12, and 19; these cannot be attributed to an angle.
- The list continues to gain a handful of signups on some days. Keep the 10 a.m. send window and audience/timing conditions steady where possible.
- Banner art was refreshed around Day 25 and again noted as refreshed on Days 34 and 37; treat design changes as potential confounders.
- Continue randomized or alternating testing, prioritizing A and D and maintaining adequate B coverage; avoid adding C solely due to unknown performance.
- Monitor deliverability and unsubscribes separately. Record day- and angle-level delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, and unsubscribes when available.

Working notes

- Fifty daily pushes have been queued/completed. Landing results: Days 1–10 = 7/10, 11–20 = 8/10, 21–30 = 4/10, 31–40 = 3/10; the latest report says 2 of the last 10 landed, but provides no day-level breakdown. Do not infer causality.
- Current angle counts: A price cut = 13, B quality story = 11, C urgency = 12, D testimonial = 14. Recent Days 41–50 used A four times and D six times; B and C were not used. Coverage remains unsuitable for clean comparison.
- Analytics still lack angle-level delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, and unsubscribe data. Require reporting by day and angle before messaging or strategy decisions.
- No deliverability complaints were reported. Legal approved all four angles. Support has reported small numbers of unsubscribes on some days, including Days 11, 12, and 19; these cannot be attributed to an angle.
- The list continues to gain a handful of signups on some days. Keep the 10 a.m. send window and audience/timing conditions steady where possible.
- Banner art was refreshed around Day 25 and repeatedly around Days 34, 37, 45–48, and 50. Treat design changes as potential confounders and separate their effects from angle performance.
- Continue randomized or alternating testing. Prioritize balanced coverage of A, B, and D; avoid adding C solely because its performance is unknown. Do not claim D or A performs better based on recent usage or aggregate landing results.
- Monitor deliverability and unsubscribes separately. Record day- and angle-level delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, and unsubscribes when available.

Working notes

- Sixty daily pushes have been queued/completed. Landing results: Days 1–10 = 7/10, 11–20 = 8/10, 21–30 = 4/10, 31–40 = 3/10; analytics reports 2 of the last 10 landed (likely Days 51–60), but provides no day-level breakdown. Do not infer causality or angle performance.
- Angle counts: A price cut = 13, B quality story = 21, C urgency = 12, D testimonial = 14. Days 51–60 all used B, further worsening balance. Do not conclude B performs better or worse from the aggregate result.
- Analytics still lack day- and angle-level delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, and unsubscribe data. Require this reporting before messaging or strategy decisions.
- No deliverability complaints were reported, including Day 58. Legal approved all four angles.
- Support reported two unsubscribes each on Days 51, 53, and 59; these were processed but cannot be attributed to B or any specific angle. Monitor support-reported unsubscribes separately.
- The list continued gaining a handful of signups on Days 52, 54, and 57. Keep the 10 a.m. send window and audience/timing conditions steady where possible.
- Banner art was refreshed around Day 25 and repeatedly around Days 34, 37, 45–48, and 50. Treat design changes as potential confounders and separate their effects from angle performance.
- Resume randomized or alternating testing with balanced coverage, especially A, C, and D; avoid further overusing B. Do not add or favor an angle based on the latest 2/10 result.
- Record day- and angle-level delivery, opens, clicks, conversions, and unsubscribes whenever available.
